name: GING
description: Ging, also called Seven Cards, is a 17th-century English declaration gambling game for four players using a 28-card stripped pack, where players claim counters for most suit points or sweeping special combinations.

content.text: Ging, also called Seven Cards, is a 17th-century English declaration gambling game for four players using a 28-card stripped pack, where players claim counters for most suit points or sweeping special combinations.
Ging is known from Francis Willughby's 17th-century game collection and is also referenced as Seven Cards.
4 players clockwise, with eldest hand left of dealer and dealer as youngest hand.
28 cards made by removing aces and cards below seven from a standard 52-card deck.
A square layout area and counters (chips).
Each player contributes two counters to dress the layout, then dealer gives 7 cards to each player clockwise.

items.text: Bankrupt End: Session can end when a player loses their last counter; remaining layout is then divided as agreed.
Fixed Number of Deals: Alternative session structure plays a predetermined number of deals and splits pool at the end.
